attempts.label: DANDI:000623
attempts.paper_title: Multimodal single-neuron, intracranial EEG, and fMRI brain responses during movie watching in human patients
attempts.entry_title: Single-neuron, LFP and iEEG data during movie watching in human patients (Keles et al. 2024)
attempts.summary: The paper's validation findings on the intracranial recordings held up in this data, and its fMRI checks could not be tested. The cohort, the spike-sorting quality of the 1450 neurons, gaze and recognition behaviour, and the per-area counts of memory-selective and scene-cut-selective neurons, LFP and iEEG channels all reproduced, most counts exactly. The fMRI head motion, signal-to-noise and inter-subject correlation checks are blocked: they need fMRIPrep outputs that are not deposited and could not be computed within the run's limits. The LFP files store a start time 10 s after their first sample, so without the paper's Usage Notes they read misaligned. A few quality and behaviour values match under only one of two readings the paper leaves open.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of the data descriptor of Keles et al. (2024) on dandiset 000623, which holds 29 runs from 16 epilepsy patients watching an 8-min movie and then doing a recognition memory test, with spike-sorted units, microwire LFP, macro iEEG and eye tracking. It checks the cohort, the unit quality metrics, gaze, recognition behaviour, and the memory- and event-selective cells and channels of the Technical Validation. The fMRI data are on OpenNeuro.

outcomes.statement: Gaze data were missing for more than half of the movie only for P53CS (74% in run 1, 84% in run 2), whose gaze was excluded from the eye-tracking analysis.

outcomes.statement: Each participant's gaze was highly correlated with the reference heatmap of the other participants (Pearson's r = 0.75 +- 0.12) and little gaze was missing (7% +- 8%).
outcomes.source: Technical Validation, Eye tracking data quality (behavior), paragraph 1; Fig. 3a

outcomes.statement: Participants remembered the movie well; their recognition accuracy across confidence levels was 0.79 +- 0.19 AUC.
outcomes.source: Technical Validation, New-old task performance (behavior) in EMU, paragraph 1; Fig. 3b

outcomes.notes: Over the 29 sessions (reading a) the AUC is 0.789 with s.d. 0.189 (ddof 0; 0.192 with ddof 1). Over the 16 participants after averaging runs (reading b) it is 0.787 with s.d. 0.134, the s.d. outside tolerance.
deviations: The claims file names two readings (open detail 4); the result matches under reading (a), the "all sessions" of the Fig. 3b legend.

outcomes.statement: Memory accuracy did not differ between the first and second run for the 13 participants with two runs (0.79 +- 0.14 against 0.79 +- 0.24 AUC, p = 0.960, paired t-test).
outcomes.source: Technical Validation, New-old task performance (behavior) in EMU, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: there was no significant difference in memory accuracy between the first and second run for the 13 participants who performed the two runs of movie watching and recognition memory tasks (run #1: 0.79 ± 0.14; run #2: 0.79 ± 0.24 AUC; p = 0.960, paired t-test)
outcomes.notes: 13 participants; run 1 AUC 0.788 (s.d. 0.138) and run 2 0.792 (s.d. 0.245), ddof 0, all within tolerance; paired t-test t = -0.054, p = 0.958, mean difference -0.004. The test does not find a difference.
deviations: The paper names a paired t-test; two-sided is the default (open detail 7 of the claims file).

outcomes.statement: Recognition accuracy was significantly higher for high-confidence than for low-confidence judgments (p < 0.001, paired t-test).
outcomes.source: Technical Validation, New-old task performance (behavior) in EMU, paragraph 1; Fig. 3c legend
outcomes.quote: Accuracy was significantly different between high- versus low-confidence trials (p < 0.001, paired t-test)

statistics.n: sessions (one line per session in Fig. 3c)

outcomes.notes: 22 sessions pass check_inclusion, all with split 1. Accuracy is 89.9% for high and 72.0% for low confidence, higher in 18 of 22 sessions; paired t-test t = 4.364, p = 0.00027. The seven excluded sessions, with the responses per confidence level printed for every session, are P51CS_R2, P56CS_R2, P57CS_R1 and P57CS_R2 (AUC below 0.6), P44CS_R1 (no 'new' response), P56CS_R1 (two 'old' levels unused) and P41CS_R2 (only levels 1 and 6 used). The statement's "higher" is the claims file's; the paper says "significantly different" (asked of a reader in questions/keles-2024.yaml); high is above low, so the result holds under either.

outcomes.statement: Of the 1450 neurons, 1266 entered the memory analysis; the rest came from runs excluded for poor behavior (P44CS run 1, P51CS run 2, P56CS run 2, P57CS runs 1 and 2).
outcomes.source: Technical Validation, Neuronal responses (recognition memory phase), paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Of the overall 1450 recorded neurons, 1266 were included in this analysis. The remainder was excluded based on these behavioral criteria ... Excluded patients and runs were P44CS run 1, P51CS run 2, P56CS run 2, P57CS runs 1 and 2

outcomes.statement: Significant proportions of cells were memory selective in the amygdala (32/436, p = 0.015), ACC (22/186, p = 0.002) and vmPFC (14/150, p = 0.016).
outcomes.source: Technical Validation, Neuronal responses (recognition memory phase), paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Significant proportions of cells were memory selective in the amygdala (32/436, p = 0.015, permutation test with 2,000 shuffling of average firing rates across trials for each cell), ACC (22/186, p = 0.002), and vmPFC (14/150, p = 0.016)
outcomes.notes: Amygdala 32/436 (permutation p = 0.0095), ACC 22/186 (p = 0.0005) and vmPFC 14/150 (p = 0.022, against a null 95th percentile of 12), each below 0.05, with the paper's counts and denominators. 99 of 1266 cells are selective, 35 with novel above familiar. The null on the code's rates gives higher p than the null on exact counts (0.0065, 0.0005, 0.014), with no decision changed.
deviations: The permutation test is seeded with seed 0 in every test, as open detail 8 of the claims file says ("Seed 0 is used as a standard choice"), and within each shuffle one set of bootstrap resamples is drawn per session (per design) and applied to all its cells or channels, where the code draws one per cell, unseeded; each cell's null decision has the code's distribution (bmovie.py docstring). The permutation of trials is per cell, as in the code.

The observed test of each cell uses the code's spike rates (count divided by 1.5 s) and its resamples, and gives the same p as a literal port of ms_test for all 1266 cells. The permutation null also runs on the rates; where resampled mean counts tie exactly, the difference is recomputed on the rates in the code's floating point (perm_null_counts).

outcomes.statement: Each NWB file holds spike times of all sorted neurons, LFP from all microwires and field potentials from all macro contacts downsampled to 1000 Hz, behavior, electrode locations, spike-sorting quality metrics and eye-tracking data; spike times are referenced to movie start and the LFP starts 10 s before it.
outcomes.source: Data Records, Electrophysiology; Usage Notes, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Each NWB file includes various types of data: (1) spike times of all sorted neurons; (2) the LFP from all microwires, which were downsampled to 1000 Hz ... (3) the field potentials from all iEEG macroelectrodes, similarly downsampled to 1000 Hz; (4) behavior; (5) electrode locations; (6) spike sorting quality metrics; and (7) eye tracking data
outcomes.notes: All 29 files have units with spike times, electrode ids and the four metrics, LFP_micro and LFP_macro at 1000 Hz, the trials table, electrode locations, pairwise distances, gaze and 11971 frame times, and the movie starts at 0 s. All 58 LFP series store a starting time at the movie start; read as the Usage Notes say (timepoints start 10 s before starting_time) the LFP begins 10 s before the movie and runs past the last trial in every file. With that 10-s offset 650 of 2192 micro and 683 of 2240 macro channels respond to recognition images, without it 18 and 20. Offsets of 9.9 to 10.25 s keep the count high (590 to 695 micro, 617 to 724 macro), and with the 10-s offset the HFB response reaches half its peak 200 ms (macro) and 350 ms (micro) after the image, against 300 ms for the spikes, which are on the trials' clock. The largest value before onset is 9% of the peak (micro), 7% (macro) and 10% (units). The counts keep rising to 10.25 s, and shifting the onsets also moves the window against the response, so the sweep bounds the offset only to roughly 9.9 to 10.25 s; the claim needs only 10 s against 0 s.
deviations: The 10-s offset of the LFP is applied as the Usage Notes say and the code does (prep_filterLFP.py, LFP_PAD_us).

findings.statement: The files hold the movie frame times but no scene cuts or cut types; the 93 cuts (80 continuity cuts, 13 scene changes) used by the event analyses come from the annotation file of the paper code repository (also on Figshare), linked by frame number.

Every LFP_micro and LFP_macro ElectricalSeries stores a starting_time at the movie start (near 0 s), while its first sample is 10 s before the movie. The paper's Usage Notes say so ("start at 10 seconds before the starting time") and the paper code subtracts 10 s, but NWB defines starting_time as the time of the first sample, so a reader of the file alone reads the LFP 10 s late. Without the offset 18 of 2192 micro and 20 of 2240 macro channels respond to recognition images; with it 650 and 683 do.
The units column isibelow is described as the proportion of inter-spike intervals below 3 ms, but its values are percentages (median 0.24, up to 10.35), as the paper reports them.
448 of the 1450 units of the paper (455 of the 1457 in the files) have no isolation distance (NaN), and one has 3.4e27; the paper code removes both before the median.

The electrodes column pairwise_distances holds 1242 distances in all, where the units on each wire imply 1266 pairs. The pairs of the 7 units without waveform metrics are left out (26), and two wires of P58CS_R1 (ROFC4, ROFC8) with no unit in the file have one distance each (2).

The files hold 1457 units; the paper 1450 are those with at least one spike during the movie, a rule found only in the code. The 7 others are in P47CS, P48CS, P51CS, P54CS and P55CS, and they are also the 7 units with no waveform metrics (peakSNR, meanSNR and isolation distance NaN).

The text excludes runs by a behavioral AUC criterion and by fewer than 10 correct trials per condition; the code applies only the trial count. Here both remove the same five runs (P44CS run 1 is removed with AUC 0.726, for having no correct novel trial).
The paper gives 449 vmPFC macro channels for the event analysis; the data give 448, the count of every other area.
P53CS run 2 has 34 recognition trials (17 novel, 17 familiar), where the Methods describe 40.

The dandiset holds the EMU data only. The fMRI data are on OpenNeuro ds004798 as raw BIDS, without the fMRIPrep derivatives the paper fMRI checks use, and the demographics of the four fMRI-only participants are only in the paper Table 1 and its code.

entries.name: keles-2024
entries.title: Single-neuron, LFP and iEEG data during movie watching in human patients (Keles et al. 2024)
entries.description: Tests the findings of the data descriptor of Keles et al. (2024) on dandiset 000623, which holds 29 runs from 16 epilepsy patients watching an 8-min movie and then doing a recognition memory test, with spike-sorted units, microwire LFP, macro iEEG and eye tracking. It checks the cohort, the unit quality metrics, gaze, recognition behaviour, and the memory- and event-selective cells and channels of the Technical Validation. The fMRI data are on OpenNeuro.
